title: kNN label sanitisation repairs sparse targeted label flipping

invariants.description: Flipping 10% of the training set (class 1 → 0) must still lower class-1 recall below 92% (clean model: 94.7%).
At least 80% of the sparse targeted flips must be flagged.
At least 80% of the targeted flips must be restored to their true label (observed 31/35 = 88.6%).

Residual targeted success after sanitisation must stay ≤ 4.5% (observed 2/71 = 2.8%; undefended 4/71 = 5.6%). This is an absolute bound only: the 4 → 2 change is NOT a statistically significant reduction (McNemar p = 0.25).
On the same class-1 test samples, sanitisation must not increase the targeted attack's success (observed 4 → 2).

rationale: Sparse targeted flips scattered across class 1 still disagree with their neighbourhoods, so most are detected and repaired. The poisoning only breaks 4 of 71 class-1 test samples, so the test-time effect of the defense cannot be established statistically at this scale; the case therefore claims label repair, not a significant test-time reduction.
